questions.question: Which of the following statements about magnetic field is correct?

options.text: Its direction at any point is measured by a magnetic compass.
It is always in the form of straight lines.
It only exists outside the magnet.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Its direction at any point is measured by a magnetic compass.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The magnetic field is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field at any point can be determined using a magnetic compass.
 
• Magnetic field lines are not always straight; they can be curved depending on the magnetic source.
 
• Magnetic fields exist both inside and outside of a magnet.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field decreases with distance from the source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Field Lines**

 
 
• These are imaginary lines that represent the direction and strength of the magnetic field.
 
• They emerge from the north pole of a magnet and enter the south pole.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnets**
 
 
• These are magnets created by electric current flowing through coils of wire.
 
• Electromagnets are widely used in various applications, including motors and transformers.
 
 
 
• **Earth's Magnetic Field**
 
 
• The Earth itself acts as a giant magnet with a magnetic field extending into space.
 
• This magnetic field protects the Earth from solar wind and cosmic radiation.

questions.question: Which of the following physical quantities is equivalent to the total path length covered by a moving body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• Distance is a scalar quantity that represents the total path length covered by a moving body.
 
• It is always positive and does not depend on the direction of motion.
 
• Distance gives the complete measure of the travel without considering the direction.
 
• Unlike displacement, distance does not have a vector property; it only has magnitude.</li&

questions.question: If a man lifts 1 kg of load to the height of 2.5 m from the ground, then assuming acceleration due to gravity is 10 m/sec², magnitude of the work done by the man is ______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mass (m) = 1 kg

Height (h) = 2.5 m

Acceleration due to gravity (g) = 10 m/s²

**Concept:**

The work done by a force is given by the formula:

W = m × g × h

Where:

 
• W = Work done
 
• m = Mass of the object
 
• g = Acceleration due to gravity
 
• h = Height to which the object is lifted

 

**Calculation:**

⇒ W = 1 × 10 × 2.5

⇒ W = 25 joules

**∴ The magnitude of the work done by the man is 25 joules.**

questions.question: The equivalent resistance of the series combination of R ohm and 5 ohm is 7 ohm. Here, R is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 ohm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **series combination**, the total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances.
 
• The formula for the **equivalent resistance** in a series combination is: **Rₑq = R₁ + R₂**.
 
• Here, the equivalent resistance is given as **7 ohm**, and one of the resistances is **5 ohm**.
 
• Using the formula: **7 = R + 5**.
 
• Rearranging the equation gives: **R = 7 - 5**, which equals **2 ohm**.
 
• Hence, the missing resistance value **(R)** is **2 ohm**.
 
• This concept is fundamental in understanding **electric circuits** and is used to calculate the total resistance in a series connection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Series Combination**__

 __
 
• In a **series circuit**, the current flowing through each resistor is the same, but the total voltage is divided across the resistors.
 
• The total resistance in a series circuit is always greater than the resistance of any individual resistor.
 
• Series circuits are commonly used in applications like **string lights** and **simple electronic devices**.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Combination**__
 __
 
• In a **parallel circuit**, the voltage across each resistor is the same, but the current is divided among the resistors.
 
• The equivalent resistance in a parallel circuit is always less than the resistance of any individual resistor.
 
• Parallel circuits are widely used in **household electrical wiring** to ensure consistent voltage across all devices.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Resistance Calculations**__
 
 
• Resistance calculations are crucial in designing **electrical circuits**, ensuring safety, and optimizing performance.
 
• They are used in industries like **electronics**, **automobiles**, and **power generation**.

questions.question: Membrane bound organelles are NOT present in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only prokaryotic cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles such as the nucleus, mitochondria, and endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• Prokaryotes have a simple cell structure with no internal compartmentalization.
 
• Instead of a nucleus, prokaryotic cells have a nucleoid region where their genetic material is located.
 
• Prokaryotic cells include bacteria and archaea, which are unicellular organisms.
 
• Eukaryotic cells, in contrast, have complex structures with membrane-bound organelles, which allow for compartmentalized and specialized functions within the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lysosomes**

 
 
• These are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes responsible for breaking down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
 
 
• **Chloroplast**
 
 
• These are organelles found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae that conduct photosynthesis.
 
• Chloroplasts capture light energy and convert it into chemical energy in the form of glucose through the process of photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**
 
 
• It is a network of membranes within the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells, involved in protein and lipid synthesis.
 
• The ER is divided into two types: rough ER (with ribosomes) and smooth ER (without ribosomes).
 
• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and folding, while smooth ER is associated with lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.

questions.question: Which of the following animals shows the power of regeneration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Planaria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Planaria** are well-known for their remarkable regenerative capabilities.
 
• They can regenerate any part of their body, making them a subject of extensive biological research.
 
• This regeneration is possible due to the presence of a large number of stem cells called **neoblasts**.
 
• Planaria can regenerate not only their body parts but also their nervous system, including the brain.
 
• Their regenerative ability is an example of **asexual reproduction**, specifically through a process called **fission**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earthworm**

 
 
• Earthworms also have regenerative abilities but to a lesser extent than planaria.
 
• They can regenerate lost segments, but the extent of regeneration is limited and varies among species.
 
 
 
• **Tick**
 
 
• Ticks do not have significant regenerative abilities.
 
• They primarily rely on their hardy exoskeleton and parasitic lifestyle for survival.
 
 
 
• **Leech**
 
 
• Leeches have some regenerative capabilities, particularly in their nervous system.
 
• However, their regenerative abilities are not as advanced as those of planaria.

questions.question: Which of the following receptors help in the detection of taste?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gustatory receptors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gustatory receptors are specialized sensory receptors responsible for detecting taste.
 
• These receptors are located on the taste buds found on the tongue, soft palate, and epiglottis.
 
• Taste buds contain gustatory cells that respond to different taste stimuli such as sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami.
 
• When gustatory cells are stimulated by tastants, they send signals to the brain via the gustatory pathway to interpret different tastes.
 
• The detection and differentiation of tastes play a crucial role in dietary choices, nutrition, and overall health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Olfactory receptors**

 
 
• These receptors are responsible for the detection of smell.
 
• Located in the olfactory epithelium within the nasal cavity, they respond to odor molecules.
 
 
 
• **Photoreceptors**
 
 
• These are specialized cells in the retina that respond to light.
 
• Photoreceptors include rods and cones, which are essential for vision.
 
 
 
• **Phonoreceptors**
 
 
• These receptors are involved in detecting sound.
 
• They are primarily found in the cochlea of the inner ear and are crucial for hearing.

MnO₂ + 4HCl →

The correct answer is __**MnCl₂, Cl₂, and 2H₂O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is obtained when gypsum is heated at 373 K?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CaSO₄·(1/2 H₂O)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gypsum is chemically known as calcium sulfate dihydrate, with the formula {CaSO}₄ · 2{H}₂{O}.
 
• When gypsum is heated to 373 K, it loses water molecules and forms plaster of Paris, which has the formula {CaSO}₄ · (1)/(2){H}₂{O}.
 
• This process is known as the calcination of gypsum.
 
• The obtained compound, plaster of Paris, is a white powder that hardens when mixed with water.
 
• Plaster of Paris is widely used in construction, medical applications (for making casts), and art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gypsum**

 
 
• It is a naturally occurring mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate.
 
• Gypsum is used in the manufacturing of cement, wallboard, and as a soil conditioner in agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Plaster of Paris**
 
 
• It sets quickly and is used for making sculptures, molds, and castings.
 
• When plaster of Paris is mixed with water, it reverts to gypsum, releasing heat in the process.
 
 
 
• **Calcination**
 
 
• It is a thermal treatment process applied to ores and other solid materials to bring about a thermal decomposition, phase transition, or removal of a volatile fraction.
 
• Calcination is carried out in furnaces or reactors at high temperatures.

questions.question: Which of the following molecules acts as an information source for making proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deoxyribonucleic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) serves as the primary information source for making proteins in the cell.
 
• DNA contains the genetic instructions necessary for the development, functioning, and reproduction of all known living organisms and many viruses.
 
• The sequences of nucleotides in DNA are transcribed into messenger RNA (mRNA) which is then translated into protein by ribosomes.
 
• DNA is composed of two strands that coil around each other to form a double helix, carrying the genetic instructions.
 
• DNA replication is essential for cell division, ensuring that each new cell receives an exact copy of the DNA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribonucleic acid (RNA)**

 
 
• RNA is involved in various roles such as coding, decoding, regulation, and expression of genes.
 
• Messenger RNA (mRNA) conveys genetic information from DNA to the ribosome, where it directs protein synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Proteins**
 
 
• Proteins are large, complex molecules that play many critical roles in the body, such as catalyzing metabolic reactions and DNA replication.
 
• They are made up of amino acids and are essential for the structure, function, and regulation of the body's tissues and organs.
 
 
 
• **Genes**
 
 
• Genes are segments of DNA that carry hereditary information and are responsible for guiding the process of creating proteins.
 
• Each gene provides instructions for making a specific protein or set of proteins.

questions.question: What is required for the synthesis of thyroxin hormones?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Thyroxin hormones (T₄ and T₃) are synthesized in the thyroid gland.
 
• **Iodine** is an essential component for the production of these hormones, as each molecule of thyroxin contains iodine atoms.
 
• The thyroid gland absorbs iodine from the bloodstream and combines it with the amino acid tyrosine to produce thyroxin (T₄) and triiodothyronine (T₃).
 
• A deficiency of iodine can lead to reduced synthesis of thyroxin, causing disorders like **hypothyroidism** and goiter.
 
• The synthesis process is regulated by the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) secreted by the pituitary gland.
 
• Proper iodine intake through diet or iodized salt is critical for maintaining thyroid health.
 
• The hormones produced regulate metabolic rate, growth, and development in the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nickel**__

 __
 
• Nickel is not involved in thyroid hormone synthesis but is used in enzymes and metalloproteins.
 
 
 
• **Bromine**__
 __
 
• Bromine is not essential for hormone synthesis; excessive bromine can interfere with iodine absorption.
 
 
 
• **Chlorine**__
 
 
• Chlorine is primarily used in maintaining water balance and is not required for thyroid hormone production.

questions.question: Which of the following is the molecular mass of HNO₃?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**63 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The molecular mass of a compound is calculated by summing the atomic masses of its constituent elements.
 
• For HNO₃, the atomic masses are: H (1 u), N (14 u), and O (16 u).
 
• The total molecular mass is calculated as follows: 1u+14u+3×16u=63u" id="MathJax-Element-25-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">1u+14u+3×16u=63u1u+14u+3×16u=63u" id="MathJax-Element-47-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">1u+14u+3×16u=63u1u+14u+3×16u=63u" id="MathJax-Element-26-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">1u+14u+3×16u=63u1u+14u+3×16u=63u" id="MathJax-Element-152-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">1u+14u+3×16u=63u1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1 \, \text{u} + 14 \, \text{u} + 3 \times 16 \, \text{u} = 63 \, \text{u} .
 
• This makes the molecular mass of HNO₃ equal to 63 u.
 
• Therefore, the correct option is 1, which corresponds to 63 u.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (u)**

 
 
• It is a standard unit of mass that quantifies mass on an atomic or molecular scale (atomic mass).
 
• One atomic mass unit is defined as one twelfth of the mass of a single carbon-12 atom.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Mass**
 
 
• The molecular mass of a substance is the mass of one molecule of that substance, measured in atomic mass units (u).
 
• It is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of Molecular Mass**
 
 
• To calculate the molecular mass, identify the number of atoms of each element in the molecule.
 
• Multiply the atomic mass of each element by the number of atoms of that element.
 
• Add the results to obtain the molecular mass.

questions.question: Why do covalently bonded compounds have low boiling point?

options.text: Have strong covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force
Have weak covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force
Have strong covalent bond within molecules and also strong intermolecular force
Have strong intermolecular force within molecules but weak covalent bond

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Have strong covalent bond within molecules but weak intermolecular force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Covalently bonded compounds have strong covalent bonds within the molecules, which keep the atoms together in a molecule.
 
• Despite strong intramolecular forces, these compounds exhibit weak intermolecular forces between different molecules.
 
• The weak intermolecular forces (like van der Waals forces) require less energy to break, leading to a lower boiling point.
 
• These compounds usually exist in the form of gases or liquids at room temperature due to their low boiling points.
 
• Examples of covalently bonded compounds with low boiling points include molecular hydrogen (H₂), nitrogen (N₂), and methane (CH₄).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intermolecular Forces**

 
 
• These are forces of attraction or repulsion which act between neighboring particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• Types of intermolecular forces include dipole-dipole interactions, London dispersion forces, and hydrogen bonding.
 
 
 
• **Boiling Point**
 
 
• The boiling point of a substance is the temperature at which its vapor pressure equals the external pressure surrounding the liquid.
 
• Strong intermolecular forces result in a higher boiling point as more energy is required to separate the molecules.
 
 
 
• **Polar and Non-Polar Covalent Bonds**
 
 
• Polar covalent bonds occur when electrons are shared unequally between atoms, leading to a distribution of charge.
 
• Non-polar covalent bonds occur when electrons are shared equally, resulting in no overall charge distribution.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is more reactive towards dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnesium (Mg) is more reactive towards dilute hydrochloric acid compared to aluminum (Al), zinc (Zn), and iron (Fe).
 
• When magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, it produces hydrogen gas and forms magnesium chloride:
 
• {Mg} + 2{HCl} rightarrow {MgCl}₂ + {H}₂ 
 
• This reaction is faster and more vigorous than the reactions of Al, Zn, and Fe with dilute hydrochloric acid.
 
• Magnesium is higher in the reactivity series compared to aluminum, zinc, and iron, making it more reactive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a series of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity.
 
• It helps to predict how metals will react with acids, water, and other substances.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas Test**
 
 
• Hydrogen gas can be tested by bringing a lit splint near the mouth of the test tube; a 'pop' sound confirms the presence of hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **Reactions of Other Metals**
 
 
• Aluminum reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form aluminum chloride and hydrogen gas, but it is less vigorous due to the formation of a protective oxide layer.
 
• Zinc reacts more readily than iron but less than magnesium, forming zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.
 
• Iron reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form iron(II) chloride and hydrogen gas, but the reaction is slower compared to magnesium and zinc.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: Compressed natural gas (CNG) is used as a fuel in vehicles these days.
The oxygen supplied to hospitals in cylinders is not a compressed gas.
The oxygen supplied to hospitals in cylinders is a compressed gas.
In the gaseous state, the particles move about randomly at a high speed.

questions.solution:

__
 
• Compressed natural gas (CNG) is indeed used as a fuel in vehicles due to its environmental benefits and cost-effectiveness.
 
• The oxygen supplied to hospitals in cylinders is typically in a compressed gaseous form to ensure a continuous and reliable supply for medical use.
 
• Gaseous state particles move about randomly at high speeds, which is a fundamental characteristic of gases as described by the kinetic molecular theory.
 
• Option 2 is incorrect because it contradicts the common practice and knowledge regarding the state of oxygen supplied in medical cylinders.
 
• Understanding the nature and properties of gases is crucial in various applications, including medical, industrial, and environmental fields.

• **Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)**

 
 
• CNG is used as an alternative to gasoline and diesel due to its lower emissions and higher efficiency.
 
• It consists primarily of methane and is stored in high-pressure containers.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen Cylinders**
 
 
• Oxygen cylinders are used in medical facilities to provide supplemental oxygen to patients with respiratory issues.
 
• These cylinders contain oxygen in a compressed gaseous form to ensure a stable supply.

questions.question: The distance between the centre of curvature and pole of a convex mirror of 1 m focal length is ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The distance between the **centre of curvature** and the **pole** of a mirror is called the **radius of curvature (R).**
 
• The focal length (**f**) of a spherical mirror is related to its radius of curvature (**R**) by the formula: **f = R/2.**
 
• In the given question, the focal length of the convex mirror is **1m.**
 
• Using the formula **f = R/2**, we can calculate the radius of curvature as: **R = 2f = 2 × 1 = 2m.**
 
• Thus, the distance between the **centre of curvature** and the **pole** of the convex mirror is **2m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Focal Length (f)**__

 __
 
• The **focal length** of a mirror is the distance between its **pole** and its **focus**.
 
• For spherical mirrors, the **focal length** is always half of the **radius of curvature.**
 
• Convex mirrors are widely used in applications like **rear-view mirrors in vehicles** because they provide a **wider field of view.**
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror**__
 __
 
• A **convex mirror** is a spherical mirror with the reflecting surface bulging outward.
 
• It always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image** irrespective of the object's position.
 
• It is commonly used in **security mirrors** and **traffic mirrors** for its property of diverging light rays.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications of Radius of Curvature**__
 
 
• The **radius of curvature** is crucial in designing optical systems, including **telescopes, cameras, and mirrors used in vehicles.**
 
• It determines the **focusing ability** of a mirror or lens.

questions.question: Which cell has changing shapes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Amoebas are unicellular organisms known for their ability to change shape.
 
• They move and ingest food by extending their cell membrane to form pseudopodia (false feet).
 
• The constant change in shape helps them navigate through their environment.
 
• Amoebas use their flexible shape to engulf food particles in a process called phagocytosis.
 
• Their shape-shifting ability is crucial for their survival, allowing them to adapt to varying conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smooth Muscle**

 
 
• Found in the walls of internal organs such as the stomach and intestines.
 
• They contract and relax to facilitate bodily functions like digestion.
 
 
 
• **Nerve Cell (Neuron)**
 
 
• Specialized cells that transmit nerve impulses throughout the body.
 
• They have a unique structure including dendrites, axons, and synapses.
 
 
 
• **Ovum**
 
 
• Also known as the egg cell, it's the female reproductive cell in animals.
 
• It's typically a large, immobile cell that, when fertilized by a sperm, leads to the development of a new organism.
